title: The Psalms, looking back
tomorrow: why would God ever tell a choir to stop singing?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Exodus: a bush on fire, a sea, bread on the ground, and commandments that open with a rescue. Out of Egypt. Now the songs people sang on the road.
screen: `OUT OF EGYPT.` → `THE SONGS ON THE ROAD.`

segments.voice: Some people keep a playlist for the bad weeks, songs that say it better than they can. One of the oldest starts in a cave. David is on the run from King Saul, who is hunting him with his soldiers, and the rock walls are close and dark. A psalm's heading puts a song right there: when he fled from Saul in the cave. Hunted, cornered, no way out but further in. And in the dark, he opens his mouth to sing. So what does a hunted man sing?
screen: `A PLAYLIST FOR THE BAD WEEKS.` → `DAVID, HUNTED, IN A CAVE.` → `WHAT DOES A HUNTED MAN SING?`

segments.voice: He starts with the truth. “Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me: for my soul trusteth in thee: yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until these calamities be overpast.” No pretending the cave is a palace. A few lines later, the song turns: “My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing and give praise.” The fear isn't edited out. It's prayed through, to the other side. Looking back, that's the pattern of the whole book. Psalm thirteen opens, “How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever?” and by its last line says, “I will sing unto the LORD, because he hath dealt bountifully with me.” Psalm thirty: “weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.” Psalm forty-two talks to itself: “Why art thou cast down, O my soul?” Anger, fear, guilt, wonder: all of it said to God rather than hidden from God. Here's one to tell a friend tonight. In Matthew's Gospel, when Jesus cries out on the cross, my God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me, he is praying the opening line of Psalm twenty-two. These are Israel's songs, still prayed in synagogues, and Christians pray them too, some in a daily round, some one psalm on a hard night.
screen: `BE MERCIFUL UNTO ME.` · `MY HEART IS FIXED: I WILL SING.` · `HOW LONG, THEN I WILL SING.` · `A PSALM FROM THE CROSS.` · then, large: `PRAY WHAT YOU FEEL.`

segments.voice: Say one line out loud, quietly, the one closest to how today actually is: how long, or why art thou cast down, or joy cometh in the morning, or I will sing. Say it twice, slowly, and let the sit hold the rest; if you pray, pray it as your own. If a feeling is too heavy to carry alone, or you're thinking of harming yourself, call or text 988 in the US, or your local emergency number.
The Psalms. Israel's book of songs and prayers, where every feeling, from how long to I will sing, is given words.
Your line: pray what you feel, the way a hunted man sang in a cave. Fourteen days into the summit.

howItsDone: Christians pray and sing the Psalms in worship, and some pray them through in a daily round of morning and evening prayer; Jews pray the Psalms in the synagogue and at home.

fork.setup: your friend's dog died this morning. she says she can't pray, because it would only be complaining. what do the Psalms offer her?
options: wait a few days, until she can pray thankfully again.
bring the complaint itself to God: how long, why. the Psalms do.
pray a cheerful psalm instead, to lift her mood first.
fork.reveal: Psalm 13 starts with how long and is still a prayer, and David's song starts with be merciful unto me. the feeling goes to God, not around God.

original.note: Hebrew: Tehillim, the name of the book of Psalms.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Psalms are polite hymns for church.
what it means: songs that carry every feeling to God, even a hunted man's fear in a cave.
what a scholar hears: some psalm headings tie a song to a scene in David's life, like Psalm 57 and Saul's pursuit in 1 Samuel; Psalm 13 moves from how long to I will sing.
guess: Israel's songs and prayers, with every feeling given words
cheerful hymns written only for church holidays
a book of rules for running the Temple

chat.says: ms. hale gave me the senior solo!! but i'm sad about leaving and it's a send-off. fake happy?
options: No. Pick a psalm that holds both: weeping for a night, joy in the morning.
Yes. A send-off needs a happy song; save the sad part for later, alone.
Skip the Psalms. They're too heavy for a school concert anyway.
chat.meaning: The Psalms pray what's actually there: David sang in the cave, and Psalm 30 holds weeping and joy together. No faking needed.

David.meaning: a shepherd who became king of Israel; psalm headings name him

Saul.meaning: Israel's king before David, who hunted him

psalm.meaning: a song or prayer from the Bible's book of Psalms

synagogues.meaning: Jewish houses of prayer and study
